evidence.exact_quote: `research_session` is a restricted `automation_session`: it reuses the same browser/runtime infrastructure but exposes a smaller action set, tighter lifecycle, and explicit escalation rules.

items.impact: Implementations have a clear class relationship and may not create a separate, more permissive research-browser runtime by implication.
items.statement: The research session class, shared infrastructure, reduced capability set, lifecycle tightening, and explicit escalation boundary are stated directly.
items.title: Research session class boundary is explicit

evidence.exact_quote: - the session is transient and tears down after the tool invocation completes

items.impact: Builders must choose what happens to browser processes, ephemeral profile data, partial evidence, annotations, and audit visibility when invocation cancellation, crash, timeout, or teardown failure interrupts the normal completion path.
items.statement: The happy-path teardown point is explicit, but abnormal termination, cleanup retry, retained evidence, privacy erasure, and user-visible recovery outcomes are not defined.
items.title: Research teardown failure semantics are missing

evidence.exact_quote: - Valid steady interaction states are `live_input`, `live_input + selection_active`, `live_input + tui_capture`, `live_input + tui_capture + selection_active` when a terminal-level selection override is intentionally engaged, `scrollback_review`, `scrollback_review + selection_active`, `scrollback_review + search_active`, and `scrollback_review + search_active + selection_active` when review selection is intentionally preserved during search. `live_input + search_active` and `search_active + tui_capture` are not normal steady states; search enters review semantics, TUI passthrough is suspended only by explicit user action, and `/history/navigation` follows the active base or `/overlay` state.

items.impact: The terminal interaction implementation and tests can reject invalid steady-state combinations without guessing from UI focus alone.
items.statement: Valid and invalid terminal interaction-mode combinations are enumerated with ownership and exit behavior.
items.title: Terminal interaction state space is testable

evidence.exact_quote: - Puppet Master supports up to two terminal sections/components.

items.impact: The third-section path, cross-window moves at capacity, restore of legacy/excess sections, and command enablement can diverge across implementations and mislead users about whether state was blocked, merged, or discarded.
items.statement: A hard terminal-section maximum is given without the deterministic command, restore, migration, or error behavior when an operation would exceed it.
items.title: Two-section limit lacks overflow behavior

evidence.exact_quote: - Retention and pruning are honest: command-history metadata is not enough by itself for review, PM preserves a bounded review transcript by default, and it does not promise infinite retention or lossless replay of arbitrary long-running PTY byte streams. The storage model separates active rendering `/input` buffer state, persisted transcript chunks for `/restore`, and lightweight command-block or session metadata keyed to transcript references; transcript persistence is append-oriented and chunked rather than one giant row or `/blob`, and `/flush` writes are batched so high-output sessions do not stall the UI thread.

items.impact: Storage sizing, pruning order, active-selection invalidation, user disclosure timing, privacy deletion, and performance acceptance cannot be implemented or falsified consistently.
items.statement: The architecture requires bounded, chunked transcript persistence but supplies no numeric default, configurable bounds, pressure thresholds, eviction order, or deterministic pruning oracle.
items.title: Transcript retention is bounded but not quantified

evidence.exact_quote: - huge-output, search, and scrollback paths remain responsive under bounded-render and bounded-memory rules

items.impact: A builder or reviewer can label materially different latency, memory, throughput, and frame-loss behavior as responsive, preventing consistent ship gating.
items.statement: The terminal acceptance criterion uses qualitative responsiveness and boundedness without workload fixtures, ceilings, percentiles, hardware classes, or failure thresholds.
items.title: Terminal performance acceptance is not falsifiable

evidence.exact_quote: - unhealthy MCP servers never produce silent success-shaped fallback

items.impact: Health polling, stale state, in-flight calls during failure, retry/backoff, user notification, and recovery authority remain builder-selected, so the anti-silent-fallback rule alone cannot guarantee consistent behavior.
items.statement: MCP unhealthy fallback is prohibited, but canonical health states, transition triggers, stale/offline behavior, retry ownership, and recovery UI are absent here.
items.title: MCP failure prohibition lacks recovery state machine

evidence.exact_quote: - close behavior must account for dirty editors, running dev sessions, active terminals, and detached children

items.impact: Concurrent dirty, running, and detached-child conditions can yield inconsistent prompts, partial closure, orphaned runtimes, or data loss because ordering, cancellation, and rollback are undefined.
items.statement: Multi-tab/window close must account for four resource classes, but no combined decision model, precedence order, atomicity rule, or partial-close recovery contract is supplied.
items.title: Workspace close orchestration is underspecified

evidence.exact_quote: - Distribution + runtime layout: per-platform runtime bundle layout, update rules, signature/hash verification with `/hash` evidence, and uninstall/removal behavior with `/removal` evidence are required for macOS, Linux, and Windows packages.

items.impact: Implementations can choose incompatible trust roots, key rotation, downgrade prevention, quarantine, failed-update rollback, and compromised-bundle recovery behavior despite the security-critical runtime distribution boundary.
items.statement: Signature/hash evidence is required, but signer authority, trust-root lifecycle, anti-rollback policy, update atomicity, verification failure states, and recovery are not defined.
items.title: CEF distribution trust and rollback remain open

evidence.exact_quote: - SMPFS-002 remains addressable as a fine-grained Section 15 PlanUnit with source-span coverage.

items.impact: The PlanUnit can pass its listed acceptance while owner/consumer behavior is incomplete or contradictory, leaving build and review closure dependent on unstated cross-document interpretation.
items.statement: SMPFS-002 acceptance checks addressability and source preservation, not observable authority-boundary behavior or reconciliation outcomes.
items.title: SMPFS-002 lacks a behavioral owner-boundary oracle

evidence.exact_quote: - SMPFS-003 remains addressable as a fine-grained Section 15 PlanUnit with source-span coverage.

items.impact: Workspace-tab project isolation, switch routing, and background-state visibility can remain untested while the PlanUnit appears accepted.
items.statement: SMPFS-003 has no scenario oracle for multiple tabs sharing a project, active-tab switching, or persistent background/blocked visibility.
items.title: SMPFS-003 shell ownership is not behavior-tested

evidence.exact_quote: - SMPFS-004 remains addressable as a fine-grained Section 15 PlanUnit with source-span coverage.

items.impact: A surface inventory may be present in prose while concrete host identity, persistence, detach/reattach, and unsupported-platform behavior remain unverified.
items.statement: SMPFS-004 accepts source-span preservation but defines no executable scenario for each primary and detached surface class.
items.title: SMPFS-004 inventory has no surface lifecycle oracle

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Browser and HTML preview are editor or workspace-tab first; the bottom panel is not the canonical browser host, and no promoted feature may depend only on floating transient overlays for navigation, review, or activity state.
- editor-area or workspace-tab first

items.impact: Downstream exact-token validation or implementation may treat `editor-area` as a supported host class even though the PlanUnit canonical text uses `editor`, creating routing and migration ambiguity.
items.statement: SMPFS-005 canonical text says `editor or workspace-tab first`, while its preserved token says `editor-area or workspace-tab first`.
items.title: SMPFS-005 introduces editor versus editor-area drift

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: A research_session is a restricted automation_session that shares browser/runtime infrastructure while enforcing tighter lifecycle, profile isolation, blocked-state visibility, and no implicit takeover of normal browsing.
gui_related: false

items.impact: GUI-oriented planning, audit, or node-readiness filters can omit the blocked-state visibility requirement and ship a runtime-only implementation with no truthful surface.
items.statement: SMPFS-006 includes blocked-state visibility in canonical text but classifies the entire unit as non-GUI.
items.title: SMPFS-006 misclassifies user-visible blocked state

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Research-session browser-action affordances consume Tools, Permissions, and UI command routing; restoring or revealing a blocked/stopped research surface returns stopped with attention_required rather than silently escalating or promoting automation.

items.impact: Restore and reveal cannot silently upgrade restricted automation authority, and the user receives an inspectable attention state.
items.statement: SMPFS-007 clearly binds research affordances to owner contracts and defines the safe stopped/attention_required restore outcome.
items.title: SMPFS-007 prevents restore-time authority escalation

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Research action tiers preserve the 15-action list, excluded action categories, annotation payloads, evidence/citation behavior, and capture-format permission boundaries including session_granted for screenshot and PDF requests.

items.impact: Builders must invent how action annotations become citations, which actions require visual evidence, how sensitive selectors are redacted, and when evidence is retained or invalidated.
items.statement: SMPFS-008 claims evidence/citation behavior but supplies no citation schema, provenance rule, privacy lifecycle, consumer contract, or acceptance oracle in the PlanUnit.
items.title: SMPFS-008 names citation behavior without specifying it

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Research session creation is implicit only for webfetch/webextract actions or webresearch fallback, remains transient unless explicitly escalated, and has no hidden takeover, promotion, or normal-browser persistence side effect.

items.impact: Automatic research fallback remains isolated and transient unless a visible authority-changing action occurs.
items.statement: SMPFS-009 explicitly prohibits hidden promotion, persistence, and takeover side effects for implicit research sessions.
items.title: SMPFS-009 fixes the implicit research lifecycle boundary

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Thread and session navigation is persistent sidebar or shell-region behavior, preserving background progress, blocked/error badges, attention surfaces, restore-and-branch lineage, and usage access without reviving floating-thread-selector canon.

items.impact: Implementations can differ on badge clearing, lineage navigation, ordering, keyboard focus, responsive collapse, and stale/error projection without violating the generic preservation acceptance.
items.statement: SMPFS-010 names persistent navigation outcomes but does not define state transitions, badge lifecycle, responsive/accessibility behavior, or scenario-based acceptance.
items.title: SMPFS-010 navigation behavior is not operationalized

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Assistant worktrees are an MVP per-project setting surfaced through chat header, thread selector icon, Source Control accordion, breadcrumb toggle, settings, and merge/test affordances without hiding project/worktree state.

items.impact: The same worktree can be represented with inconsistent identity, state, actions, enablement, or failure disclosure across six surfaces, especially during merge tests and concurrent project activity.
items.statement: SMPFS-011 inventories worktree surfaces but does not specify their shared projection, command payloads, state synchronization, error behavior, or acceptance scenarios.
items.title: SMPFS-011 lists surfaces without a shared worktree contract

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Assistant worktree integration preserves GitHub Integration, WorktreeGitImprovement, FinalGUISpec, Orchestrator/Source Control, and chain-wizard owner splits, consumes the current seven-tab Orchestrator shell from Orchestrator_Page, and keeps Non-MVP exclusions from becoming implicit MVP behavior.

items.impact: Section 15 consumers are constrained from silently re-owning worktree lifecycle, Source Control, Orchestrator structure, or non-MVP behavior.
items.statement: SMPFS-012 explicitly preserves cross-owner boundaries and fixes the consumed Orchestrator shell shape.
items.title: SMPFS-012 preserves worktree owner splits

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Thread context detail preserves the active-thread context indicator, compact rows, Deep Plan, usage/tokens/cost hover, Compact Now, and editor-tab Context Detail Pane while rejecting a detached usage pop-out as canonical.

items.impact: Keyboard-only, touch, screen-reader, and reduced-pointer users may not receive equivalent Usage, Tokens, Cost, or More Details access; localized expansion may also break compact-row assumptions.
items.statement: SMPFS-013 canonizes hover disclosure without defining an equivalent focus, activation, assistive-technology, touch, or localization behavior and without an accessibility oracle.
items.title: SMPFS-013 context disclosure lacks non-hover equivalence

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: The terminal is the canonical interactive shell surface with up to two terminal sections, tab and pane layout families, bottom-default placement, detach/move/resize behavior, labels, and settings vocabulary.

items.impact: Capacity overflow, detach failure, invalid move targets, ratio restoration, and concurrent close/move operations remain discretionary even though the PlanUnit spans multiple stateful behaviors.
items.statement: SMPFS-014 compresses a broad terminal surface state machine into one canonical sentence and generic source-preservation acceptance without scenario outcomes.
items.title: SMPFS-014 terminal surface behavior is too coarse to test

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Terminal runtime identity preserves terminal_section_id, terminal_tab_id, terminal_pane_id, terminal_session_id, and dev_session_id owner splits; presentation changes must not mint runtime identity and dev_session_id is not a shell-session alias.

items.impact: Consumers can distinguish presentation continuity, exact PTY continuity, and dev-workflow continuity, preventing duplicate or silently substituted shell sessions.
items.statement: SMPFS-015 explicitly assigns identity ownership and prohibits presentation operations or dev-session aliases from minting or impersonating PTY identity.
items.title: SMPFS-015 identity boundaries are explicit

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Terminal presentation containers preserve labels, roles, settings precedence, tab/pane motion, reveal/move/rename/pin/close/detach/reattach behavior, and requested/effective disclosure without changing runtime identity.

items.impact: Commands may disagree on stale target handling, concurrent move/close resolution, requested/effective payload shape, focus preservation, and rollback after detach or reattach failure.
items.statement: SMPFS-016 lists presentation operations and disclosure goals without per-command preconditions, result states, conflict rules, failure outcomes, or executable acceptance scenarios.
items.title: SMPFS-016 presentation commands lack outcome contracts

segments.summary: Reviewed shell ownership, research-session action tiers and lifecycle, worktree and usage surfaces, terminal identity, presentation, interaction states, selection, and command-block prelude; found strong class and state boundaries but missing abnormal teardown and terminal-section overflow contracts.

Reviewed terminal command metadata, lifecycle, restore, requested/effective state, stable identities, attention routing, promoted feature requirements, pane ownership, persistence tiers, platform capability matrix, and architecture; key gaps are unquantified retention/performance, incomplete MCP recovery, and non-transactional close semantics.

Reviewed terminal architecture and observability, browser runtime/actions/profiles/artifacts/permissions/distribution, persistence and anti-drift rules, plus SMPFS-002 through SMPFS-004; found a critical browser-runtime supply-chain gap and PlanUnit acceptance criteria that validate migration shape rather than observable behavior.

Reviewed SMPFS-005 through SMPFS-010 line by line; confirmed explicit research restore and lifecycle boundaries, while finding editor/editor-area token drift, a GUI classification conflict, undefined citation/evidence behavior, and unoperationalized persistent navigation requirements.

Reviewed SMPFS-011 through SMPFS-016 and the assigned continuation context; confirmed owner and runtime-identity boundaries, while finding missing shared worktree contracts, non-hover context-detail access, coarse terminal-surface acceptance, and unspecified presentation-command outcomes.
